### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **36** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**36** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1b329d8d491bbfbde882385858dfde18b575469c` — the merge of head `624045a8e6610fb1c264116851f274d6314e1510` into base `82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1b329d8d491bbfbde882385858dfde18b575469c && git checkout 1b329d8d491bbfbde882385858dfde18b575469c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 624045a8e6610fb1c264116851f274d6314e1510 && git checkout -B drift-repro 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 && git merge --no-ff 624045a8e6610fb1c264116851f274d6314e1510

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `5f673cafd4933e97ba8ee7f49d15f2cd98401d41`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

- **Declaration face.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: two `advisory`-tier rules, `validateEmailTemplateDefaultArguments` (CLI and runtime, `runtimeTypes: ['email_template']`) and `validateNotifyTemplateVariables` (CLI only, `RUNTIME_NEEDS_FULL_SNAPSHOT`), plus their exports. Neither is `gating`, so nothing that saved, built or validated before is refused. At the publish door the first rides the save response as an advisory through the existing `runtimeTypes` path. That is additive. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no key, value or type an author writes moves. `@objectstack/lint: patch` is correct for a non-protocol widening. The four doc rule counts move from 65 to 67 to match.
- **Default-argument rule.** It considers only holes `parseMailHole` parses with formatter `default` and no refusal, and skips quoted or empty arguments. It flags an `@`-marked path, a dotted path, a name the template uses as a variable, or a snake_case name. A plain word like `Customer` is not flagged unless the template uses that name as a variable. The message and hint follow ruling 6845318122 B ("a default is literal text; compute it in the flow").
- **Notify rule.** It runs only for a `notify` node whose `template` names a template the stack declares and whose `templateData` is absent or an object. `required` is read per locale member, and the locales are named when not all members require the variable. A root key holding a CEL envelope counts as supplied, as do `appName`, `baseUrl` and `email.defaultTemplateContext` keys. A dotted key (`'task.title'`) is correctly not read as a path, and the hint says so. It warns rather than refuses because a host can add context in code. That is the right tier.
- nit N1: `mayBeSupplied` treats a CEL envelope as supplying only at the root or at the leaf. `templateData: { task: { meta: <envelope> } }` with `task.meta.x` required is reported as missing, a false positive for an advisory. Treating an envelope at any segment as supplied would close it.
- nit N2: the doc example fix (`'task.title'` → `task`) corrects a send that always failed. Worth a line in the release notes, since authors may have copied it.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/lint: patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, per AGENTS.md (non-protocol change ships `patch`).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Area A2. The PR is still a draft.
